# WO-602: Say "not checked" instead of "found" for brokers that were never searched
Status: queued (in-house)
Vendor: claude
Agent: automation-engineer (Theo Park); CLI wording: orchestrator (contract)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Kind: engine
Tier: deep
Severity: HIGH
Target release: 0.4
Source: owner real-data test, stage 1 (search only), qa-security 2026-11-11. Private results are kept outside the repo; this WO is PII-free by rule.

## Goal
On the owner test (full registry, 424 enabled brokers, no searchable broker, see WO-601) `freemyid scan` finished in 5 seconds and printed "<label>: found: 423". Every one of those is a blind broker set to FOUND with reason `presumed_listed` (`engine/runner.py:638-643`); nothing was seen. `RunReport.summary_lines` (`engine/runner.py:142-153`), `status` and the dashboard chip all say "found". A non-technical user reads that as "my details are on 423 sites", which is false and alarming, and it hides the fact that no search ran.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. The run summary separates "found on the site" (a scanned listing) from "not checked, we will ask anyway" (blind/presumed). Plain words, no state names.
2. `run/1` JSON gains a per-profile `presumed` count (or equivalent) so scripts can tell them apart; documented in docs/CLI.md (orchestrator: `cli.py`/`cli_json.py` are contract files).
3. `status` and the dashboard show a distinct label for presumed-listed brokers (wizard text change goes to wizard-packager).
4. When a scan searched zero brokers, the summary says so in one line ("No site could be searched automatically; requests will still be sent.").
5. Tests: blind registry -> summary has no "found" line; mixed registry (one fake searchable broker with a fixture, one blind) -> counts split correctly. Events stay ids/enums/counts.
